newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends higher, but strength ebbs.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends higher, but strength ebbs.

text.p: Shares closed higher on Wednesday in a pale imitation of the surge in Wall Street overnight, trimming early gains as many investors remained cautious and brokers said the mood was still fragile.
The HEX index closed up 0.83 percent at 2,851.64 with volume at 490 million markka, more sturdy than of late but still below start-of-year levels.
"The U.S. rise did not quite convince this market," one said. "There weren't many buyers."
Nokia managed to rise back through the psychological 300 markka barrier, but was off a four-week high of 309.50, ending up 2.00 at 302.00 and making up about one-fifth of total volume.
Brokers said many investors were on hold ahead of Q1 reports from Sweden's Ericsson on Friday and Nokia itself next Tuesday.

But Helsinki was not totally devoid of its own drivers and some brokers said the expiry of FOX stock futures may help boost trade on Thursday: "I expect arbitrage-related buying to take us into positive ground," one said.
Aamulehti was again lively, firming early on to make an assault on 200 markka in the wake of its planned merger with local broadcaster MTV, but then landing down 3.00 at 187.00.
"People thought that (200.00) was a bit high so they came in and took profits. I think that will remain the ceiling, at least for the while. It's quite a tough level," one broker said.

Kemira, ex a 1.60 markka dividend, fell 1.70 to 51.30 with brokers seeing some pressure in a slightly muted 1997 profit outlook from Tuesday. Kemira repeated it saw full-year earnings almost matching 1996, but said January-April would be weaker.
UPM led forestries, rising 2.00 to 115.00 in solid volume.
